fields.why: Figure notes say 'Estimates for vaccination intent are not shown for groups with sample size <30', a suppression of observed values, which the brief classes as transformation; A records it as ancillary, B misses it.

Sex is one of the weighting control totals ('age group, sex, metropolitan statistical area status, education...'); the brief records sex whenever it appears, so B's sex (covariate) belongs, without raising the level.

The Discussion credits 'programmatic measures that helped reduce disparities ... such as making vaccines available free of charge' and nontraditional settings, offering cost and access as explanations of a change in the racial disparity, not only as a recommendation; A's reading of it as a recommendation is defensible but weaker.

'Coverage with all vaccines was lowest among uninsured persons' ranks insurance groups with a superlative, which looks groupwise; the brief says to record anything that looks groupwise, and Figure 2's category count is unavailable, so n_groups null is right.

Methods state 'Differences among estimates were determined using t-tests', so the race (White vs others) and rurality (urban/suburban vs rural) claims rest on pairwise tests against a referent; only the age gradient ('increased with age') is side by side. A itself marks race resolves_to_finer true and t-tests primary, which contradicts 'side by side'.

brief_issues: The brief does not say whether 'higher/lower' claims under a blanket 'differences were determined using t-tests' count as pairwise assessments (per-group vs referent) when the referent is unnamed ('most other racial and ethnic groups'); a rule saying a stated pairwise test makes the assessment 'per-group vs referent only' would settle it.
